newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales slow at $66 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales slow at $66 - trade.

text.p: Feedlot cattle sales in the central and southern Plains on Friday were slow following active sales on Thursday, feedlot and government sources said.

About 300 head of steers expected to grade select to choice sold in Kansas at $66.00 per cwt, USDA said. The price was steady with the bulk of this week's trade although USDA on Thursday reported a few pens of cattle sold at $66.25.
Cattle prices posted in Nebraska were higher than in areas to the south, with USDA reporting sales early Friday there at $67.00 per cwt on a live basis and $110.00 on a dressed basis.

Most feedlots in Kansas, Texas and western Oklahoma remain current following this week's brisk trading, with Kansas moving 83,900 head and Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area movement confirmed by USDA at 62,400.
However, Nebraska sales at 26,800 this week fell short of the projected showlist.
Fed cattle prices next week were expected steady-firm amid ideas that many feedlots were continuing to market cattle two to three weeks ahead of schedule, feedlot sources said.
The early marketings were reflected in latest estimated average market weights which remain well below a year ago.
Weights were still low despite record-breaking warm temperatures in the southern Plains that should be favorable for weight gains, sources said.

Average estimated weights on steers and heifers slaughtered under federal inspection for the week ended Saturday were 1,163 lbs compared with an estimated 1,166 the previous week and well below the actual 1,209 lbs recorded last year, according to USDA in its latest U.S. meat production report.
